params.body:
An audit of the gates between Explore, Signal, Decode and Intelligence on every surface: web pages, `/api/v1`, MCP tools, report files. Rapporten (PDF and page images), sources on the trend page and the daily allowance were sound. These were not.

**1. The trend graph named concepts and patterns to everyone.**
- The trend page wrote the whole graph into its HTML for every visitor, signed in or not. The API and the MCP tools rightly keep concepts and patterns for Decode and up (the Graph ability).
- `Reader::graphFor` now keeps the shape and the counts for everyone. Below Decode, concepts, patterns and tensions lose their names and their name-bearing ids (swapped for `n1`, `n2`, and the edges follow). Signal sources stay the Sources ability.
- The graph script shows an unnamed node as its layer.
- Tests: `PlanTest` (Explore and Signal see no names, Decode sees all), `InsightGraphTest` (the page HTML).

**2. One archive rule.**
- Signal's blurb says "the whole archive" but its window was 90 days. Signal now opens all of it, here in the site's fallback offer and in gentells-pipeline #249.
- `archiveCutoff()` follows a trial (and the freemium switch) the way `may()` does. A trial listed the archive among its abilities and was refused it on the next call.
- A single post past the window still gives the teaser through every door, as the web does, so nothing leaked there.

**3. Token grants and evidence links.**
- `readsPremium()` ignored the token's granted scopes while the freemium switch was on. A client approved for the latest posts only got whole bodies, the Opportunity and the evidence. It now uses the same grant check as `may()`.
- The three teaser signals under a post went out with their url to every reader. Where a signal comes from is the Sources ability, so urls now come from Signal up.

**4. The two doors count alike** (`Meter`).
- Only answered reads use the allowance. A refusal ("this needs Decode") is still written down, but no longer counted; the API never counted one and MCP did.
- An MCP call that finds nothing writes no read, as an API 404 never did.
- A trend opened by an old address (alias) and by its current one is one trend for the sources brake.
- Test: `MeterFairnessTest`.

**5. Team accounts.**
- The team login (#170) now marks the account `team = true`, like the team reconcile does. Leaving the team on the pipeline therefore also ends it here.
- New column `plan_before_team` (migration): joining the team keeps the plan someone had, and leaving gives it back instead of dropping to Explore.
- Tests: `TeamReconcileTest`, `TeamLoginTest`.

On production `premium_requires_plan` is on and billing is not live, so the freemium paths are dormant there. Points 1 and 3 applied today.

Tests: 366 passing, 7 new. Pint clean.
params.title: Gates: one rule per ability across the page, the API and MCP
